text:
Alex K: Pager triggered — high error rate on inference route in us-west-2 and an unusual S3 access pattern that matches our log exporter. not sure if it's read or write.
Maria P: seeing repeated 403->200 flips for S3 objects under rdinference-exports/sessions/. digging now.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • High • 1805123456 • Assigned to Oncall Ryan • PagerDuty
Oncall Ryan: I can take. initial triage: suspension of the log-exporter job? we should limit blast radius. pinging eng-lead and legal.
Eng Lead Sara: Agreed. Pause the exporter via the control-plane flag: `redwoodctl exporter pause --name=session-shipper --region=us-west-2`
Alex K: doing that now. FYI I see ~12k GETs over the last 30m from a single AWS principal. IPs are varied but ASN resolves to a hosting provider.
Maria P: quick grep of object ACLs — looks like a subset of session-metadata files had `AuthenticatedUsers` ACL on creation by an older batch job (created 03/2024). probably a regression from a library change.
Oncall Ryan: Important: are these files user content or just metadata pointers? if no PII, lower severity for customer notices, but still need disclosure.
Eng Lead Sara: These are session metadata (session_id, model_version, request headers, partial prompt hashes). There may be user-supplied text in early experiments for some customers — we need scope.
CS Jordan: preparing a notification template but need scope confirmed before sending.
Legal - Priya: Hold on outreach. We need a scoped statement for affected customers and an internal timeline. do not confirm exposure beyond what we can verify.
Maria P: I'm running a selective scan for files that contain suspicious patterns (email regex, JWT-looking strings, long prompt text). returning matches in a minute.
Alex K: pausing public read perms on the bucket as mitigation: `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket rdinference-exports --acl private` — applied. will monitor for further GETs.
incident-bot: ACTION LOG • 1805123490 • exporter paused • bucket ACL set to private
Maria P: initial scan: ~380 objects with plain-text-looking prompts or email addresses. many of these are internal test data, but ~27 objects appear to include user-provided prompts > 200 chars.
Eng Lead Sara: ok, that's non-trivial. escalate to sec/privacy. Priya — please advise on disclosure thresholds.
Legal - Priya: If customer data was accessible even for a subset, we should prepare: (1) an internal impact summary, (2) a tailored notice for affected customers, (3) a public status page update if broader impact. We'll need exact scope before customer list.
Oncall Ryan: I'm generating an export of object keys and their creation principals to hand to legal/CS. pushing to a secure bucket `rd-incident-exports/1805123456` with restricted access.
Alex K: note — the export contains object previews; redacting by default. use `gzip` + KMS: `aws s3 cp preview.json s3://rd-incident-exports/1805123456/preview.json --sse aws:kms`
CS Jordan: Draft customer notification (do not send yet):

```
Hello <CustomerName>,

We detected a configuration issue that may have made a limited set of session metadata files temporarily readable. We are investigating which files were affected and whether any customer-provided text was present. At this time we have paused the exporter and restricted bucket access. We will follow up within 72 hours with scope and recommended actions.

— Redwood Inference Incident Response
```

Legal - Priya: good start. tighten: remove definitive language about "may have" -> use "may have been accessible" and include hotline for security contact. Also include a timeline placeholder.
Alex K: timeline so far for internal record:
- 1805123120 — exporter job updated (deploy)
- 1805123300 — anomalous S3 GET pattern begins
- 1805123420 — pager triggered
- 1805123456 — incident created in slack
- 1805123490 — mitigation: exporter paused, bucket ACL set to private
- 1805123550 — initial scope scan underway

Maria P: I'm attaching a short grep sample (redacted) for the privacy team to review: `session_preview_snippet: "<redacted user prompt snippet>"`
Legal - Priya: Next steps checklist for internal comms and customer outreach:
- Confirm exact object keys and customer mapping (Eng)
- Verify whether any PII or credentials were present (Privacy)
- Draft per-customer tailored notices (CS + Legal)
- Prepare a neutral public status page update if > 1 customer or if systemic (Ops)
- Postmortem and remediation plan commit (Eng)

Eng Lead Sara: For status page language draft (Ops team can refine):

```
We are investigating a limited data exposure affecting a subset of session metadata files in our rdinference-exports bucket. We have restricted access and paused the exporter. We'll provide more details as our investigation confirms scope and impacted customers.
```

CS Jordan: Will prepare per-customer language variants:
- Variant A: Confirmed exposure of customer-provided prompts — include recommended rotation steps if credentials exposed.
- Variant B: Potential exposure of metadata only — provide summary and reassurance about minimal risk.
- Variant C: No customer data found — notification of incident and confirm no action required.

Oncall Ryan: Handing over to the daytime response crew at 08:00 PST — assigned to Alex and Maria for next shift. please use `#incidents` for updates and `#incidents-private` for any attachment with PII.
Alex K: acknowledged. leaving a runbook note: `runbook/exports-acl-fix` entry created and linked.
incident-bot: HANDOFF • 1805123589 • Pager reassigned to Daytime Response • Oncall Ryan -> Alex K
Legal - Priya: once the Eng export is ready, send to me + CS + Privacy group. I will review and OK customer notices. Do not send anything public until legal signs off.
CS Jordan: Understood. I'll draft Variant B now and drop in this thread for review.
Eng Lead Sara: Good job on quick mitigation. keep updates coming on the scope numbers and any confirmed PII. we'll prepare a post-incident action item list (immediate: harden exporter, add CI check for ACLs, rotate keys used by exporter if any).
Alex K: Update in 15."
